description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its comforting warmth and rich, earthy flavor. This hearty soup is often seasoned with a vibrant mint and paprika infused butter, adding a beautiful color and aromatic depth. It's a staple in Turkish homes, perfect for a nourishing meal any time of year.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrot, and potato. Saute for 5-7 minutes until the vegetables soften.

instructions.title: Add Tomato Paste and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for another minute, stirring constantly. Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine with the vegetables.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable or chicken stock. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Return the pot to low heat. Season the soup with salt, black pepper, and dried mint. Stir well and let it gently warm through for 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Mint Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the red pepper flakes and a pinch of dried mint. Cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the warm mint and red pepper butter over each serving. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

tips: For a truly authentic taste, do not skip the mint and red pepper infused butter topping. It adds a crucial layer of flavor and aroma.
If you prefer a thinner soup, you can add a little more hot stock or water after blending to reach your desired consistency.
Mercimek Corbasi tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
article:
Mercimek Corbasi, a name that rolls off the tongue with the promise of warmth and comfort, is much more than just a soup. It's a culinary embrace, a staple found on almost every Turkish table, from bustling city restaurants to cozy family homes. This humble yet incredibly flavorful dish, known as Mercimek Corbasi, is the quintessential Turkish Red Lentil Soup, celebrated for its smooth texture, vibrant color, and incredibly satisfying taste.

Imagine a bowl of creamy, bright orange-red goodness, steaming gently, offering a subtle aroma of earthy lentils, sweet vegetables, and a hint of minty spice. That's the magic of Mercimek Corbasi. It's a dish that transcends seasons, equally cherished as a comforting meal on a chilly evening or a light, nutritious starter during warmer months. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a beginner in the kitchen, preparing this beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a rewarding journey that brings a piece of Turkish culinary heritage right to your home. In this comprehensive guide, we'll dive deep into the world of Mercimek Corbasi, exploring its ingredients, step-by-step preparation, pro tips, and how to serve it like a true Turk.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-MEK chor-BAH-suh," translates directly to "lentil soup." However, in Turkey, when one refers to "lentil soup" without specifying, they almost always mean the red lentil version. It's more than just a soup; it's a culinary hug, a staple that embodies the warmth and hospitality of Turkish cuisine, making it the most iconic Turkish Red Lentil Soup.

The soup's characteristic vibrant orange-red hue comes from the red lentils themselves, which break down beautifully during cooking, creating an incredibly creamy texture without the need for any dairy products. This makes it naturally vegan (when prepared with olive oil) and gluten-free, appealing to a wide range of dietary preferences. Its flavor profile is a delicate balance of savory and subtly sweet, thanks to the combination of sautéed onions, carrots, and sometimes potatoes, enhanced by a touch of tomato paste and a medley of spices. Often, it's finished with a drizzle of *nane yağı* (butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes), which adds a crucial layer of aromatic depth and a beautiful visual flourish. It's nourishing, easy to digest, and incredibly versatile, solidifying its status as a beloved Turkish classic.

## Ingredients You Need

The beauty of a classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup lies in its simplicity and the quality of its fresh ingredients. You don't need exotic items to create this masterpiece; rather, it’s about combining everyday staples to unlock extraordinary flavor.

*   **Red Lentils:** 1 cup (about 200g) – The star of the show. Make sure they are split red lentils, as they cook faster and break down more easily for that smooth consistency.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, chopped – Forms the aromatic base, adding sweetness and depth.
*   **Carrot:** 1 medium, chopped – Contributes natural sweetness and color.
*   **Potato (optional but recommended):** 1 small, peeled and chopped – Adds body and a velvety texture, making the soup even more satisfying.
*   **Garlic (optional):** 2 cloves, minced – Enhances the savory notes.
*   **Tomato Paste:** 1 tablespoon – Provides umami, richness, and a deeper red color.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** 2 tablespoons – For sautéing the vegetables.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** 6-7 cups (1.5-1.75 liters) – The liquid base. Broth adds more flavor.
*   **Salt:** 1 teaspoon (or to taste)
*   **Black Pepper:** 1/2 teaspoon (or to taste)
*   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** 1 teaspoon – Essential for the authentic Turkish flavor profile.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Pepper):** 1/2 teaspoon (or to taste) – For a gentle warmth and color.
*   **For the Nane Yağı (Mint Oil) Topping:**
    *   **Butter:** 2 tablespoons (or olive oil for vegan option)
    *   **Dried Mint:** 1 teaspoon
    *   **Red Pepper Flakes:** 1/2 - 1 teaspoon (adjust to your spice preference)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Creating your own Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward and enjoyable process. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl every time:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrot, and potato (if using). Sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables soften and the onion becomes translucent. If using garlic, add it in the last minute of sautéing to prevent burning.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Spices:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for another 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step is crucial as it deepens the flavor of the tomato paste. Then, add the dried mint, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper. Stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
4.  **Combine with Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot. Pour in 6 cups of water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend Until Smooth:** Once the lentils and vegetables are cooked through, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. Add the remaining 1 cup of water or broth if the soup is too thick for your liking, and bring it back to a gentle simmer. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
6.  **Prepare the Nane Yağı (Mint Oil) Topping:** While the soup is simmering or just before serving, prepare the topping. In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes. Sizzle for about 30 seconds, being careful not to burn the spices. The mint will become fragrant, and the butter will turn a beautiful reddish hue. Remove from heat immediately.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Turkish Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Drizzle a generous spoonful of the fragrant *nane yağı* over each serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is easy with a few insider tricks. These tips will help you elevate your homemade Mercimek Corbasi from good to truly exceptional.

*   **Rinse Those Lentils!** We can't stress this enough. Rinsing thoroughly not only removes impurities but also helps prevent the soup from becoming overly starchy and cloudy.
*   **Sautéing is Key:** Don't rush the sautéing of the vegetables. Allowing the onions, carrots, and potatoes to soften and lightly caramelize builds a crucial flavor base for the soup. Cooking out the tomato paste also deepens its taste.
*   **Blend for Creaminess:** The signature velvety texture of Mercimek Corbasi comes from a thorough blending. Whether you use an immersion blender or a regular one, ensure the soup is completely smooth with no discernible lentil pieces.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentils absorb a lot of liquid. As the soup cools, it will thicken. Feel free to adjust the consistency with more hot water or broth when reheating or if you prefer a thinner soup.
*   **Don't Skip the Nane Yağı:** The minty butter topping, *nane yağı*, is not just a garnish; it's an integral part of the Mercimek Corbasi experience. It adds an incredible aroma, a pop of color, and a burst of authentic flavor that truly completes the dish.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving. Salt, pepper, and even a little extra dried mint can make a big difference in balancing the flavors. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end can also brighten the entire soup.

## Serving Suggestions

Serving your Turkish Red Lentil Soup correctly can truly enhance the experience, transforming it from a simple dish into a delightful culinary event.

*   **Lemon is Essential:** A wedge of fresh lemon is the most traditional accompaniment. A squeeze of lemon juice brightens the soup's flavor, adding a tangy counterpoint to the rich lentils.
*   **Crusty Bread:** Serve with plenty of fresh, crusty bread (like a baguette or Turkish *pide*) for dipping. It's perfect for soaking up every last drop of the delicious soup.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or mint over the top, in addition to the *nane yağı*, adds a touch of freshness and color.
*   **Pickles and Olives:** In Turkey, it's common to serve soup alongside a small plate of assorted pickles (*turşu*) and olives, which offer a delightful tangy crunch.
*   **As a Starter or Main:** Mercimek Corbasi makes an excellent starter for any Turkish meal, preceding kebabs or other main courses. It's also hearty enough to be a light, satisfying lunch or dinner on its own, especially when paired with bread and a simple salad.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, it also offers a fantastic canvas for creative variations and substitutions to suit different tastes or dietary needs.

*   **Add More Vegetables:** Feel free to experiment with other vegetables. Diced bell peppers, celery, or even zucchini can be added alongside the carrots and onions for extra nutrients and flavor.
*   **Spice It Up:** If you prefer a bolder flavor, consider adding a pinch of cumin or a touch of smoked paprika to the soup base. For more heat, increase the amount of red pepper flakes in both the soup and the *nane yağı*, or add a fresh finely chopped chili pepper.
*   **Broth Boost:** While water works perfectly, using vegetable or chicken broth will undoubtedly add a deeper layer of umami and richness to your Mercimek Corbasi.
*   **Vegan/Dairy-Free Topping:** For a completely vegan version, simply use olive oil instead of butter for the *nane yağı* topping. The flavor will still be fantastic.
*   **Creamier Texture:** For an even richer, silkier texture (though not traditional), some recipes call for a splash of milk or cream at the very end, after blending. However, the beauty of this Turkish Red Lentil Soup is its natural creaminess from the lentils.
*   **Garlic Lover's Version:** Don't be shy with the garlic! Adding an extra clove or two, minced, during the sautéing stage can give the soup a more pungent, robust flavor.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a recipe; it's a testament to the power of simple ingredients coming together to create something truly extraordinary. Its nourishing qualities, comforting warmth, and delightful flavors make it a beloved dish across Turkey and increasingly, around the world. Whether you're seeking a healthy weeknight meal, a soothing bowl for a chilly day, or an authentic taste of Turkish cuisine, this iconic red lentil soup is guaranteed to satisfy. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to fall in love with the comforting embrace of Mercimek Corbasi.
